questions.problem: Find the numbers $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=24{x}^{2}+20x+4$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $7.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 7 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(24{x}^{2}+20x+4)\,\text{d}x \\ 7 & ={\frac{1}{c}(8{x}^{3}+10{x}^{2}+4x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 7 & =\frac{1}{c}[(8{c}^{3}+10{c}^{2}+4c)-0] \\ 7 & =8{c}^{2}+10c+4 \\ 0 & =8{c}^{2}+10c-3 \\ 0 & =(2c+3)(4c-1) \\ c & =-\frac{3}{2},\,\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $c>0,$ we conclude that $c=\frac{1}{4}$ only.

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi -0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{8}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We calculate this integral using a substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{8}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{-1}{u}^{8}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{\frac{1}{\pi }(\frac{{u}^{9}}{9})|}_{1}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9\pi }[(-1)^{9}-{1}^{9}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{9\pi }(-2) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14199393/assets/dfa665cf99f35e5cd2edef04b3f334f0054bbce7fc9b66c519d59d30e77ba2a1.png)

The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[0,10],$ is shown above. It consists of line segments.

Find the average value ${f}_{\text{avg}}$ of $f(x)$ on $[1,9].$ Do not round the answer.

${f}_{\text{avg}}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{1}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{5}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,5].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-4.
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [5,9].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
{\int }_{5}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x={A}_{2}=6.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =-4+6 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9-1}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
